faq: Where will my product be hosted?

On a service that fits your stack, such as Vercel, Render, Fly.io or a cloud server, always in an account you own. We explain the monthly cost before we set it up, and the provider bills you directly.
Can you launch a product someone else built?
Yes, if we can read the code and run it. We check the project first and tell you honestly if it needs fixes before it is safe to put online. That review is part of the work.
Do you handle the Apple or Google store launch?
No, this service covers web products. Mobile app store submissions are a separate service, and approval is always up to the store. We follow the store rules and never promise a result.
What if something breaks after launch?
Within the support window in your package we investigate and fix problems that come from our setup or the code we touched. After that, ongoing care can be quoted as a separate monthly arrangement.

desc:
SaaS product launch and deployment support moves your product from a developer's machine to reliable hosting, with a domain, HTTPS, backups and alerts. Ecom Swift LLC sets it up in your own account and stays on hand while your first customers arrive.

## What is SaaS launch and deployment support?

Deployment means putting your application on servers where the public can reach it. Launch support is the wider set of tasks around that moment: connecting a domain, securing it, backing up the database, watching for errors and being ready to fix problems when real users show up.

A product can work perfectly on a laptop and still fail on launch day because an environment variable is missing, an email provider is not configured or the database has no backup.

## Why launch week goes wrong without preparation

Launches are rushed. The code is finished late, the domain is not pointed correctly, and nobody has checked what happens when ten people sign up at once. Problems that a calm checklist would have caught appear in front of your first customers, who may not return.

Silent failures are worse than loud ones. If the product throws an error and nobody is alerted, the first you hear about it is a complaint, or nothing at all because the user simply left. A proper setup tells you first.

## How a prepared launch protects your first impression

Early customers decide quickly whether a product feels dependable. A site that loads over HTTPS, on your own domain, with working sign-up emails, looks like a real business. Error tracking and uptime checks shorten the time between a failure and a fix, and a daily backup means a mistake does not become a disaster.

A staging site gives you somewhere to test changes before real users see them. A support inbox with reply templates helps you answer the first questions calmly. Together these reduce the stress of launching and keep your attention on customers instead of firefighting.

## What a good launch setup includes

- Production hosting in an account you own.
- Your domain connected, with a valid HTTPS certificate.
- Environment settings and secrets stored safely, not inside the code.
- A scheduled database backup, with a note on how to restore it.
- Error tracking that reports problems with enough detail to fix them.
- Uptime checks that email you when the site stops responding.
- Sign-up and email delivery tested from a clean account.
- Analytics and sign-up tracking verified.
- A staging copy for safe changes.
- A launch checklist that records what was checked and by whom.

## How we support the launch

We review the product, choose hosting that suits it and deploy it from your repository. We connect the domain, turn on HTTPS, switch on backups and walk through the launch checklist with you. On launch day we watch the alerts and fix small problems as they appear.

The Basic package covers deployment, domain, HTTPS, backups and the checklist. Standard adds error tracking, uptime alerts, launch day cover and a few quick fixes. Premium adds a staging site, support inbox and templates, tracking checks, a longer period of fixes after launch and a review call. Load testing and a public status page are optional extras.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Test sign-up, login and any payment from a fresh account on launch eve.
- Keep a written list of every service your product depends on.
- Turn on backups before the first real customer arrives.
- Decide who receives alerts and what they do when one arrives.
- Plan a quiet first week with no big new features.

**Avoid:**
- Launching on a Friday evening with nobody available.
- Storing passwords and keys in the code repository.
- Sharing one hosting login among several people.
- Changing the live site directly without a staging test.
- Assuming a backup works before trying to restore from it.

## Who this service is for

Founders whose product is finished but who have never deployed one will gain a guided, calm launch. Teams who built with a freelancer and received only code need someone to place it online properly. Founders who launched quietly and now expect more traffic want monitoring in place before it arrives.

## What we need from you

Your repository as a collaborator, a hosting account you create and add us to as a team member, your domain and a list of third-party services such as email and payments. We never need your passwords. If the product is for the Apple or Google app stores, tell us at the start, because that process works differently.
